issues.description: The commented example in the template Main uses two-argument constructors for animals (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), but the problem text and the intended design (Animal has only a name) and the solution use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal(String name)). This discrepancy between the template's example usage and the specified/implemented constructors can confuse students about the required constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's example usage consistent with the specification and solution. Update the commented constructors in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if a second attribute is intended, update the problem statement and solution to declare and initialize that attribute across Animal and subclasses.

issues.description: The template's Main.java sample code constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")). However, the problem description/UML specifies that animals have a single 'name' attribute (constructors should initialize class attributes), and the reference solution implements single-argument constructors (Seal(String), Pig(String), Goat(String)). This signature mismatch (two-arg vs one-arg) can confuse students about the expected constructor for these classes and how the UML/problem maps to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the sample usage in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java with the UML/problem and solution by using single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors were intended, update the problem statement/UML and implement matching constructors in the solution/template classes so all artifacts use the same constructor signature.
